title: Ezekiel Bible Quiz - Chapter 6
description: Ten questions on Ezekiel 6: the word against the mountains of Israel, the high places and the remnant that escapes.

questions.text: Toward what was he told to set his face and prophesy?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:2 tells him to set his face toward the mountains of Israel and prophesy to them.

answers.text: The siege works around Jerusalem
The land of the Chaldeans
The river Chebar
The mountains of Israel

questions.text: Besides the mountains and the hills, what else does this word address?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:3 says the Lord Yahweh speaks to the mountains and to the hills, to the watercourses and to the valleys.

answers.text: The seas and the islands
The trees and the fields
The watercourses and the valleys
The cities and the villages

questions.text: What does he say he will destroy when he brings a sword on them?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:3 says, "Behold, I, even I, will bring a sword on you, and I will destroy your high places."

answers.text: The walls of Jerusalem
Their high places
The gates of the temple
Their fields of grain

questions.text: What does verse 4 say will happen to their altars and their incense altars?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:4 says their altars will become desolate and their incense altars will be broken, and he will cast down their slain men before their idols.

answers.text: The altars will be desolate and the incense altars broken
The altars will be carried to Babylon
The incense altars will be left standing
Both will be covered with earth

questions.text: Where does he say he will scatter their bones?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:5 says he will lay the dead bodies of the children of Israel before their idols and scatter their bones around their altars.

answers.text: In the valleys
On the mountain tops
Around their altars
In the streets of the city

questions.text: When the slain fall among them, what will they know?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:7 says the slain will fall among them, and they will know that I am Yahweh.

answers.text: That the prophet spoke his own words
That he is Yahweh
That the nations are stronger than they
That Yahweh has forsaken the land

questions.text: What will those who escape do among the nations where they are carried captive?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:9 says those who escape will remember him among the nations, and will loathe themselves in their own sight for the evils they have committed.

answers.text: Remember him and loathe themselves for the evils they committed
Build new altars among the nations where they go
Forget the land of Israel and all its mountains
Rejoice that they alone were delivered from the sword

questions.text: What was he told to do with his hand and his foot, and what to say?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:11 says, "Strike with your hand, and stamp with your foot, and say, 'Alas!'" because of the evil abominations of the house of Israel.

answers.text: Clap his hands and sing a song to the mountains
Lift up his hands and bless the house of Israel
Cover his face and keep silent before them
Strike with his hand, stamp with his foot, and say "Alas!"

questions.text: According to verse 12, what happens to the one far off, the one near, and the one who remains besieged?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:12 says he who is far off will die of the pestilence, he who is near will fall by the sword, and he who remains and is besieged will die by the famine.

answers.text: The sword for the one far off, famine for the one near, pestilence for the besieged
Pestilence for the one far off, the sword for the one near, famine for the besieged
Famine for all three alike
Pestilence for the one near, the sword for the besieged, escape for the one far off

questions.text: How far does he say he will make the land desolate and waste?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:14 says he will stretch out his hand on them and make the land desolate and waste, from the wilderness toward Diblah, throughout all their habitations.

answers.text: From Dan to Beersheba, throughout all their cities
From the river Chebar to the land of Babylon
From the wilderness toward Diblah, throughout all their habitations
From the great sea to the mountains of Judah
